transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

On Samsung washers, 4C means the machine isn't getting enough water within the expected time. A dry drum fits that. It's often something simple, so work through these in order:

1. Check the tap
• Make sure the supply tap behind/under the machine is fully open. These isolation valves often get knocked half-closed or seize partly shut. If it's a lever type, the handle should be in line with the pipe.
• Check that other taps in the house have normal pressure. If there's work on the mains or a pressure drop, that'll do it.

2. Check the inlet hose
• Pull the machine out and make sure the hose isn't kinked or crushed behind it. This is very common after the machine's been moved or "walked" during a spin.

3. Clean the inlet filter (most likely culprit)
• Turn the tap off, then unscrew the hose from the back of the machine (have a towel or bowl ready).
• Inside the inlet on the machine there's a small mesh filter. They clog with limescale and grit, especially in hard-water areas.
• Gently pull it out with pliers, rinse under a tap, and use an old toothbrush if needed. Refit it, reconnect the hose hand-tight plus a little, and check for leaks.
• Check the tap end of the hose too. Some have a washer or mesh there as well.

4. Test the supply directly
• With the hose disconnected from the machine, point it into a bucket and briefly open the tap. You should get a strong flow. If it's a trickle, the problem is the tap or hose, not the washer.

5. Reset the machine
• Switch off at the wall for a minute or two, then try a short cycle (e.g., Rinse + Spin).

6. Listen when it starts
• When the cycle begins you'd normally hear a click and the hiss of water entering.
• If you hear a hum or click but no water, even with good supply, the water inlet valve has likely failed.
• If you hear nothing at all, it could be the valve, wiring, or the control board.

If none of that works
A faulty inlet valve is the next most common cause. It's a fairly cheap part, and replacing it is a modest DIY job if you're comfortable unplugging the machine and taking the top panel off. Otherwise an engineer will usually do it quickly. Less commonly, the pressure sensor or main board is at fault.

Before calling anyone: check whether you're still under warranty or have cover through your home insurance or the retailer. Also, the SmartThings app's diagnostics (if you've paired the machine) can sometimes give more detail.

Nine times out of ten it's the tap, a kinked hose, or that inlet filter, so it's worth 15 minutes of checks first.

Tap was open, and I turned it fully anticlockwise anyway, no change. Kitchen cold tap pressure is normal and the hose isn't kinked. When it should be filling I get a faint buzz/hum from the back but no water sound. I took the hose off and the mesh filter was clogged with grey grit and limescale bits. I cleaned it and refitted, and now it fills normally and the 4C has gone.

Good result. The buzz/hum makes sense now: the inlet valve was opening as it should, but the clogged filter stopped water getting through. So the valve is fine and you won't need a call-out.

A few follow-ups:

• Check for leaks at both ends of the hose over the next couple of washes. Look especially at the machine end, where the filter sits. Hand-tight plus a quarter turn is usually enough. If it weeps, check the rubber washer is seated flat.
• Check the tap end of the hose if you didn't already. Some hoses have a second mesh there that can clog too.
• Where did the grit come from? A sudden load of grey grit often follows water mains work, a burst main nearby, or plumbing work in the house disturbing sediment. If it was a one-off, you're probably sorted. If it keeps building up, an inline filter on the supply could be worth fitting.
• Hard water: if you're in a hard-water area, check and clean the filter every 6–12 months. It takes two minutes and prevents a repeat.
• Run a drum clean (Samsung's "Drum Clean" or "Eco Drum Clean" programme) if it's been a while. It helps with general limescale and odours.

If 4C comes back soon after a clean filter, there's more sediment upstream. Check the isolation tap itself and the tap-end mesh.
